subject: ancient-history
topicName: The Fall of the Roman Republic

questions.question: Q: Why were the Gracchi brothers killed?

points.text: Tiberius Gracchus proposed land reform to redistribute public land to the poor, threatening wealthy senators' interests. He bypassed the Senate and was beaten to death by senators. His brother Gaius continued the reforms but was also killed. Their deaths showed the Republic could not reform peacefully.

questions.question: Q: How did Marius' military reforms undermine the Republic?

points.text: Marius opened the army to the landless poor (capite censi) and made soldiers swear loyalty to their general, who provided pay, land and booty. This created private armies loyal to commanders rather than the state, enabling men like Sulla and Caesar to use military force against Rome itself.

questions.question: Q: What was the First Triumvirate and why did it collapse?

points.text: An unofficial alliance of Caesar (military reputation), Pompey (military glory and influence) and Crassus (wealth) formed in 60 BC to control politics. It collapsed after Crassus died at Carrhae (53 BC) and Caesar's growing power alienated Pompey and the Senate, leading to civil war.

Senators led by Brutus and Cassius feared Caesar was becoming a king, which was anathema to Republican values. He had been declared dictator for life, his image appeared on coins (previously only gods), and he received extravagant honours. The conspirators believed killing him would restore the Republic; instead it triggered more civil war.

questions.question: Q: Why did the Roman Republic fall?

points.text: Multiple causes: growing inequality between rich and poor, the Gracchi showed reform was impossible peacefully, Marius' military reforms gave generals private armies, the Senate proved unable to govern effectively, and ambitious men (Sulla, Caesar) used military force against Rome. The Republic's institutions could not handle the strains of empire.
